comparison: Perfect alignment (100% claim overlap: C14-C20, C85-C86). Both evaluations support these background claims about substrate channeling based on cited structural and functional literature. Neither evaluation challenges these established findings from prior studies.

Both address the main conclusion about SC function (C9, C10, C92, C96) but diverge in evaluation. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on comprehensive experimental evidence. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN due to Reviewer 2's concerns about mechanistic understanding and generalizability to other systems, despite acceptance by other reviewers.

Both address baseline D. melanogaster SC characterization with partial overlap (C5, C27, C29, C32, C33, C39). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval covers broader claim set including structural mechanisms (C36) and detergent sensitivity (C31, C34), while peer review focuses on core observational findings.

Substantial overlap on introductory/contextual claims (C1-C4, C11-C13, C23-C26, C28). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R1 integrates these with experimental data on D. melanogaster SC formation, while peer R8 treats them as accepted background without challenge.

Both address increased SC formation in perturbation models (C7, C43, C44, C47, C48) and both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative assessment across strong/mild perturbations. Peer review explicitly confirms convincing evidence that SCs form in mutants but not wild type.

Both address functional consequences of SC formation (C8, C49, C52, C53) and both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes respirometry data showing no functional enhancement and equal CI/CII-linked respiration. Peer review confirms SC abundance changes do not impact respiratory function as key validated finding.

Overlap on functional analysis claims (C59, C65-C68). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R4 focuses on Bcs1 knockdown showing respiration increase less than CI activity increase. Peer R3 broadly accepts functional characterization across all models.

Overlap on biochemical characterization of knockdown models (C55, C57, C58). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R4 covers comprehensive Bcs1 phenotype data. Peer R6 validates technical quality of experiments across all three knockdown models.

Minor overlap on respirasome-like structure formation (C61, C62). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R4 discusses this in context of mild Bcs1 knockdown. Peer R2 confirms SC formation in mutants as convincing finding.

Overlap on Ndufs4 strong knockdown functional deficits (C77, C78, C83). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R5 provides detailed characterization of differential effects between strong/mild knockdown. Peer R3 accepts functional characterization broadly.
Overlap on biochemical characterization (C72, C73, C76). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R5 covers Ndufs4 knockdown phenotypes. Peer R6 validates technical quality of experiments across models.

Overlap on mild perturbation approach (C79, C80). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R5 emphasizes mild Ndufs4 knockdown showing increased SC without functional deficits. Peer R7 validates graded perturbation experimental design.

Overlap on mild Coa8 perturbation (C45, C46). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R2 provides quantitative evidence for increased SC in mild knockdown. Peer R7 accepts graded perturbation approach without challenge.

Both address structural explanations for D. melanogaster SC organization (C88-C91). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R8 integrates these with evolutionary arguments but rates overall result as UNCERTAIN due to speculative assembly kinetics hypothesis. Peer R9 accepts structural claims based on cited literature without challenge.

Both address assembly kinetics hypothesis (C93-C95). Both rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval R8 notes this is speculative with limited comparative data. Peer R10 confirms this is hypothesis rather than demonstrated finding, with indirect questioning via generalizability concerns.
Minor overlap on evolutionary context (C21, C22). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R8 includes these in broader discussion of structural/evolutionary explanations. Peer R8 treats as accepted background.
Overlap on field context and species variation (C3, C23). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R9 focuses on state of field regarding SC function debate. Peer R8 treats as accepted introductory context.
Minor overlap on strong Coa8 knockdown characterization (C42). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R2 provides detailed quantitative evidence. Peer R6 validates technical quality of experiments.
Minor overlap on mild Bcs1 perturbation (C60). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R4 covers comprehensive Bcs1 phenotype. Peer R7 accepts graded perturbation design.
Minor overlap on mild Ndufs4 SC formation (C82). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R5 emphasizes this as important for overall conclusion. Peer R2 confirms SC formation in mutants.
